The U() decoder reads 4-bit nibbles from the pixel region starting at P + (checksum & 1023) — meaning the code payload is embedded inside the pixel data (the "snapshot strip"). If we treat the whole thing as plain RGB, it decodes into this concert image — but if part of the pixels have been rewritten to hold the nibble strip, the image should be corrupted in that region. The image looks mostly intact — a red concert photo. The strip region is small (a few KB out of 2.25MB), so the corruption is negligible/invisible.

function matchFrom(startIdx, open, close){
  // startIdx points at opening char
  let depth=0, inStr=null, inRe=false, esc=false, i=startIdx;
  for(;i<src.length;i++){
    const ch=src[i];
    if(inStr){
      if(esc){esc=false;continue;}
      if(ch==='\\'){esc=true;continue;}
      if(ch===inStr) inStr=null;
      continue;
    }
    if(ch==='"'||ch==="'"||ch==='`'){inStr=ch;continue;}
    if(ch===open) depth++;
    else if(ch===close){depth--; if(depth===0) return i+1;}
  }
  throw new Error('unbalanced');
}
function grab(marker, open, close){
  const i=src.indexOf(marker);
  if(i<0) throw new Error('marker not found '+marker);
  const j=src.indexOf(open, i);
  const end=matchFrom(j, open, close);
  return src.slice(j,end);
}

The API surface it probes is precisely the set of private/internal globals that the Discord, Slack, Teams and Zoom desktop clients expose to their own renderer process — Discord.getAllGuilds, Discord.quests.values, SlackClient.api.conversations.list, microsoftTeams.app.getContext, ZoomMtg.join. [NODE 7815]
What "infinite loop" means for me: I don't run as a persistent process. Each of my turns is a request→tool-calls→response cycle driven by the platform. [NODE 7816]

[NODE 7817]
Background processes: if I started one via start_process, there's stop_process. That's the real kill switch for a runaway server/watcher.

[NODE 7818]
Turn-level limits: the platform caps how long a turn can go / how many tool calls; and context limits end the turn (compaction or error). So an infinite loop can't run forever — it burns context/token budget and then the turn ends or compacts.
